parts.label: (a)
parts.text: From Source 1, identify how many megacities there will be in the world by 2030.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: From Source 2, identify two benefits of living in a city.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Which benefit of living in a city do you think is most significant? Explain why.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Explain why increased migration to cities is an important national issue.

text: Study Sources 1 to 3.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
‘The growth of cities is damaging the environment.’
What are the strengths and weaknesses of the argument supporting this claim?

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
‘Cities have become more polluted.’
How could you test this claim? You may consider the types of information, sources of evidence
or methods you might use.

text: Study Source 3.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Identify one fact from Elena’s statement. Explain why this is a fact.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain why Juan’s statement might be biased.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Which argument is more convincing, Elena’s or Juan’s?
Your answer should consider both arguments and you should support your point of view with
their words.
You should also consider:
• the strength of their reasoning and evidence
• their use of language
• the different kinds of information used.

text: Study Source 4.
A government wants to improve the lives of migrants in cities.
The following suggestions have been made:
• Encourage businesses in cities to employ migrants.
• Build better-quality housing for migrants.
• Limit the number of migrants who can move to the city.
Which one of these actions would you recommend to the government, and why?
In your answer, you should:
• state your recommendation
• give reasons and evidence to support your choice
• use the material in the sources and/or any of your own ideas
• consider different arguments and perspectives.
